class_guess: Sync bouncer counter: binary counter on the left, eroding 1-block timer on the right, doubling reset
summary: Left binary counter +1 per visit; right 1-block loses 2 cells/visit, pad gains 4; reset doubles it. Digit grammar open
mechanism: Each visit (right record in C) maps `0^inf L 1^n 0^g C> 0^inf` to `0^inf inc(L) 1^(n-2) 0^(g+4) C> 0^inf`: the head stripes the block going left, adds 1 to the counter L, zigzags back and erases the block's last 2 cells (early in a phase, filler cells of L can merge into the block).

inc is a binary +1: the carry depth follows the ruler sequence (27,084/27,124 visits). Digits are 1 or 2 cells, separated by `00` gaps or 1-runs the carry passes; the layout is rebuilt at each reset and migrates early in a phase (the open part).

Reset at n=2: `L0 0 1^2 0^g C>` -> `L0 1^(g+6) C>` with g = 4(visits-1), so the block about doubles. All 12 resets to 2.5e9 hit a bit-0 = 0 visit; 35/36 off-sync variants leave an odd pad and halt next visit. Not a cryptid: plain +1, linear timer.

template.diff: 11 of 12 transitions differ: a class-level match, not a delta
template.note: Same macro shape (left binary counter, right side reset in sync, progress_nonhalt_cond). TM4's fixed digit words d0/d1 and BC.Mul2 do not fit: here digits are 1 or 2 cells with phase-dependent fillers. No solved machine within 3 transitions (nearest: CTLv1, RWL_mod, CPS_LRU deciders at 4).

strategy:
Visit-level proof: invariant = L in a counter language K (with bit-0 alignment to the block), g = 0 mod 4.
Prove V for L in K from S, P, Z and per-digit carry lemmas; R for the reset (plus the absorption visits); then progress_nonhalt_cond.
Open: write down K (digit/filler grammar) and prove it closed under inc and the reset, including the sync.
risks: The counter's digits (1 or 2 cells) and fillers change layout at each reset and migrate early in a phase; the grammar K is not pinned, and its closure is the proof.

Sync: all 12 resets landed on a bit-0 = 0 visit, but visits per phase are not always odd (phase 5: 104, after 10 absorbed cells). 35/36 off-sync resets halt on the next visit (tested), so the sync must come out of the grammar.
No close template (SBCv7/SBCv11 are class-level only): expect a long custom .v, kill #4-sized or larger.

checkpoint_questions.text: Fig 1: does each white triangle read as one phase (the block eaten from its right while the black pad grows), ended by a full-width white row (the reset), each phase about twice as wide as the last?
Fig 2: reading each row right to left from the white block, do the flickering columns form a binary counter (the rightmost column flips every row, the next every 2 rows, then every 4, 8, ...)?

Confidence is med: the open part is the counter's digit grammar (1- or 2-cell digits, fillers that shift each phase). Should we spend a deepen stage pinning that grammar and its closure, or park this machine behind the others?
